t: This is the Hardy Tree, in the churchyard of St Pancras Old Church. It was an ash tree, and what made it famous is the stacked gravestones embedded around its base. It was listed among the Great Trees of London in 2008. It's named for Thomas Hardy, the novelist and poet, who also trained as an architect. Hardy wrote as a Victorian realist, and he was critical of Victorian society, especially its treatment of rural people in his native South West England. Look at the gravestones gathered around the base.
